classification.difficultyReason: Determine scale intervals and units, account for the syringe scale decreasing toward the nozzle and read a temperature below zero.

content.prompt: The diagrams below show the readings for measurements taken using different measuring tools. The arrow indicates what the measurement was in each case. Read each scale and write down the reading. Include the unit of measurement.

spec.description: Ruler segment with one-millimetre subdivisions, longer five- and ten-millimetre ticks, and a downward red indicator. Decorative blue pattern omitted.
spec.mathematics: Labels 80 through 150 in steps of 10; indicator at 120; unit mm.
spec.answerVisibility: Scale values and indicator are permanent givens; no answer text is added.

answer.worked: Each small interval represents $1\text{ mm}$. The arrow points to the labelled $120\text{ mm}$ mark.

spec.description: Measuring jug with spout, right handle, five equal intervals between consecutive labelled marks, and liquid surface aligned with the indicator.
spec.mathematics: Major labels 0, 250 and 500 ml; each minor interval is 50 mL; liquid and arrow at 250 mL.
spec.answerVisibility: Liquid level, graduations and indicator remain visible; no answer text is added.

answer.worked: The arrow and liquid surface align with the $250$ mark. The reading is $250\text{ mL}$.

spec.description: Syringe with nozzle pointing right, slightly raised towards the right. Scale decreases from left to right. Decorative barrel colouring omitted.
spec.mathematics: Labels 20 ml, 15, 10, 5, 0 with one-millilitre graduations; upward arrow targets 4.
spec.answerVisibility: All source scale labels and the indicator are permanent givens.

answer.worked: The scale decreases towards the nozzle. Each small interval represents $1\text{ mL}$, and the arrow points one interval to the right of $5$. The reading is $4\text{ mL}$.

spec.description: Vertical thermometer with right-hand Celsius scale, red bulb and liquid column, and a leftward arrow at the liquid level.
spec.mathematics: Labels 20, 10, 0, -10, -20 and -30; one-degree subdivisions; liquid and arrow three subdivisions below zero.
spec.answerVisibility: Liquid level and indicator are visible; no reading is supplied as answer text.

answer.worked: Each small interval represents $1^{\circ}\text{C}$. The indicated level is three intervals below zero, so the reading is $-3^{\circ}\text{C}$.
